is_featured.name: How to Choose the Right Indoor Plants
is_featured.subtitle: A Room-by-Room Guide to Greenery
is_featured.description: Indoor plants do more than decorate. They purify the air, soften edges, and bring calm energy into a room. This guide offers a practical approach to selecting plants that match each space’s unique light, moisture, and layout. With a basic understanding of plant behavior and room conditions, it becomes easier to create lasting, beautiful indoor greenery.
is_featured.img_alt: indoor room setup with potted plants on windowsill shelf and floor in cartoon style jpeg

is_featured.name: How to Choose the Right Engineered Wood
is_featured.subtitle: 8 Types for Every Project
is_featured.description: Choosing the right wood board can make or break your project. Literally. Engineered boards like plywood, MDF, and particle board may look similar in the store, but they behave very differently when you start cutting, screwing, or finishing them. This guide breaks down eight common types of engineered wood with real-world pros, cons, cost, and ease of use. Whether you're a DIY beginner or seasoned woodworker, you'll know exactly what to pick for your next project.
is_featured.img_alt: distinct wooden tile samples neatly arranged each tile has a unique grain or color pattern jpeg

is_featured.name: How to Pot or Re-pot a Plant
is_featured.subtitle: A Minimalist’s Guide to Plant Care
is_featured.description: In pots, plants can't rely on nature to do the heavy lifting. Soil gets stale, roots hit walls, and hidden pests can cause damage. Repotting mimics the natural cycle, refreshing soil, renewing nutrients, and giving roots space to grow strong. It’s one of the simplest ways to keep your plants thriving, disease-free, and growing beautifully, even in a contained space.
is_featured.img_alt: cheerful plant in cracked pot with big eyes and exposed roots next to clean new pot tiny trowel and fresh soil minimalistic cartoon style jpeg

is_featured.name: Common Electrical Disasters
is_featured.subtitle: A Minimalist's Guide to Electrical Wiring
is_featured.description: Electrical issues like melting plugs and tripping breakers often start small but can lead to serious hazards. This simple, beginner-friendly guide explains common wiring mistakes and how to prevent them using practical tips for a safer home setup.
is_featured.img_alt: overheated power socket with smoke electrical safety cartoon flat minimal style jpeg

is_featured.name: The One Step Rule
is_featured.subtitle: How to Accomplish Anything Without Burnout
is_featured.description: Most of us believe big achievements come from doing a lot of things every day. But real progress happens by completing just one small, meaningful task—something that directly pushes a goal forward. Trying to do everything at once can be overwhelming, but focusing on just one essential task each day leads to consistent growth over time.
is_featured.img_alt: hand placing brick on small growing wall minimalistic colorful cartoon jpeg

is_featured.name: Dal ‘n Spinach
is_featured.subtitle: A Simple Vegan Comfort Curry
is_featured.description: A warm, creamy, and mildly spiced dish that combines the earthy richness of lentils with the fresh vibrance of spinach and the warmth of aromatic spices. Every bite delivers a comforting blend of nuttiness and creaminess without being too sweet or overly spicy. Packed with protein and fiber, this wholesome meal pairs perfectly with rice, roti, or even quinoa.
is_featured.img_alt: minimalist cartoon style illustration blended yellow dal shredded spinach cilantro garnish fine dining plating flat colors black outlines top down view jpeg

is_popular.name: Add Tailwind CSS to Next.js
is_popular.subtitle: Quickly In 4 Steps
is_popular.description: Recent versions of Next.js come packaged with Tailwind CSS, which we can enable during project creation. If you missed installing it out of the box, this guide will walk you through four simple steps to install and configure Tailwind CSS. Even though this post is tailored for Next.js, a similar method can be used to set up Tailwind in a React.js application as well.
